title: Satyavati
body:
Satyavati

Satyavati's origins were steeped in cosmic mystery and divine design. In the kingdom of Uparichara, a fisherman caught a massive fish in the Yamuna. When the fish was cut open, the fishermen found twin children, a boy and a girl. They took the children to their king. The king chose the boy to be brought up in his household, and he later went on to found the kingdom of Matsya (meaning fish).
The girl, who possessed a fishy odor, was given to the chief of the fishermen to be raised. She was Satyavati. As a young maiden, she assisted her father by running a ferry service across the Yamuna. One day, the great sage Parasara wanted to cross the river and availed himself of her services. Midway through the crossing, the sage was seized with a sudden longing for the beautiful maiden. He expressed his desire to her.
Satyavati was both flattered and frightened. She raised several objections, mentioning her fishy odor, her unwedded status, and the open light of day where they could be seen by the sages on the banks. Parasara, through his yogic power, created a dense mist that enveloped the boat, hiding them from view. He then granted her two boons: that she would regain her virginity immediately after their union, and that her fishy odor would be replaced by a divine perfume that would emanate from her and pervade the forest for miles.
From this union, Satyavati gave birth to a child on a misty island in the Yamuna. This child was Sage Vyasa, the great compiler of the Vedas and the author of the Mahabharata. Vyasa immediately grew into maturity, bowed to his mother, and departed with a solemn promise: 'Whenever you call upon me in times of difficulty or need, I shall return to assist you.'
Years went by, and King Shantanu, who had kept his senses under strict control since Ganga left him, was wandering on the banks of the Yamuna. Suddenly, the air was filled with a fragrance so divinely sweet that the king sought its cause. He traced it to Satyavati, whose divine perfume now pervaded the entire forest. The sight of this beautiful maiden burst the bonds of his restraint, and filled him with an overmastering desire to make her his wife.
